name: LLNL Biotech Summer Experience
org: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) Science Education Program
what_you_do: A free two-week lab workshop at LLNL. Students work on a molecular biology and bioinformatics project, studying genes from a duckweed plant.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 11 or 12 at a Northern California high school (public, charter, private or homeschool). Must be 16 or older at the start. GPA 3.3 or higher and science GPA 3.5 or higher. Must have finished Biology and Chemistry (or Integrated Science I and II). Students 18 at the start must be U.S. citizens.
pay_detail: Free to attend. Lunch is not provided.
duration: Two weeks. In 2026: weekdays July 13 to 24, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened Jan 19, 2026, student deadline Feb 26, 2026 (11:59 p.m.), recommendation letter due March 6, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet. Expect a January opening again.
how_to_apply: Online application, your latest high school transcript (unofficial is OK), and contact info for your Biology or Chemistry teacher, who sends a recommendation letter.
notes: Competitive, and space is limited. You must be allowed to enter the Lab under federal law (2025 NDAA Section 3112), which blocks some foreign nationals. Bring your own laptop and get your own ride. Contact: stem-education@llnl.gov.
